summary: Year 3 Engineering student at the University of Cambridge, specialising in Information and Computer Engineering, with hands-on experience in low-level firmware engineering at Arm, full-stack development, machine learning research, and agentic AI systems. Skilled in C/C++, Java, Python, and TypeScript, with expertise spanning secure boot firmware, scalable web applications, predictive ML models, and LLM harness workflows including RAG, MCP, and context engineering.

experience.description: Kernel, security, and isolation layer development for Arm's next-generation CPU platform, working on low-level C firmware and secure boot engineering.
achievements: Developed kernel, security, and isolation layer firmware in C performing CPU integrity verification at power-on and establishing hardware-backed security layers prior to OS handoff
Engineered secure bootloader: cryptographically verify Linux image integrity and detect unauthorised modifications, safeguarding the trusted boot chain from power-on to Linux launch
Profiled and refined performance-critical code paths, substantially improving runtime efficiency across the pre-boot software stack
Collaborated cross-team within Arm's engineering workflows, leveraging CI/CD pipelines and standard testing tools to validate firmware reliability

Applied Git workflows and collaborated with senior engineers in both in-person and remote settings
